AgentCompass v0.7.1 lets a route you name launch past the automatic-routing switches, brings back reference data published between releases, and gives every model and effort a host offers a value by a declared method. It builds on v0.7.0.

- **A route you name launches.** `allowed_accounts` and the model checkbox decide what automatic routing may pick. A route named with `--provider/--account/--model/--effort --basis "<your words>"` launches past them; facts still refuse it (an exhausted window, a model the account does not serve, a failed login). The gate governs dispatch only: a message to a worker that is already running is not a dispatch and is not gated.
- **Reference data published between releases reaches installs.** v0.7.0 removed the between-release channel. This release restores it in a narrower form: the maintainer publishes a set on purpose (`agentcompass data publish`, written to `published/<schema>/` on `main`), an install fetches the set of its own data schema, accepts it only when this version's readers load it and an offline plan completes with it, and otherwise keeps the set it shipped with. `agentcompass data` shows which set is in effect. Off switch: `AGENTCOMPASS_PUBLIC_DATA=off`, or `{"enabled": false}` in `~/.agent-compass/public-data-config.json`. The boards are still read once per release; what moves between releases is a new model, a corrected hand-written score or a corrected launch row.
- **Every offered model and effort has a value.** For each model and effort the shipped launch table and the Cindy and Magpie gateways offer, every facet, Time/Task and cost per hour is a reading or an estimate by a declared method with its inputs shown: a same-line relative by version distance, another line of the same maker and product by median or extrapolation, a tier fit, effort steps measured on the boards' own listings. The order of methods follows leave-one-out error. Efforts run from `none` to `ultra`; a value never rises against the effort order or exceeds a strictly larger model of the same product and not older version, and an estimate moves before a measurement does. What has no value is on a known-gap list with a kind from a closed set. At this release: launch table 176 of 176, Cindy 381 of 399, Magpie 687 of 743 pairs; the rest are listed gaps (22 of them names a provider now serves with other weights than the row).
- **Fleet fits are frozen per release.** Tier fits, effort and size steps, Time fits, the cost ratio between sources, level targets and the panel scale are computed from the release's rows only. `agentcompass data refresh --model <id>` scores a new model by those fits and changes no other row; a row whose readings are part of the release's fits is refused until the next release. Generated files no longer hold the time they were written, so a rebuild on another day is byte-identical.
- **Models and identities.** Gemini 4 Neon is in the data with four Antigravity launches (low to xhigh). `gpt-6-pro` (Pro in ChatGPT) is no longer a model of its own: it is GPT-6 Astra at one operating point above Max, with a declared response floor of 600 s; a hand-written score for it never reads below Astra at that point. Its Time/Task rises from 8.8 to 33.6 minutes at High. The calibration panel takes `muse-spark-1.3` in place of `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`, which no single snapshot lists on every core board. The aliases `gemini-4-pro` and `gemini-4-ultra` are removed; `claude-opus-5`, `claude-sonnet-5` and `claude-fable-5` are rows of their own instead of aliases of the current models; DeepSeek's dated snapshots are rows of their own; `kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed` is one row.
- **What you wrote under an earlier name is kept.** A manual score stored under a name v0.7.0 resolved through an alias, with or without a provider prefix, moves to the row v0.7.0 meant (`user-scores.json` schema 4). A model you unchecked keeps its checkbox: a stored choice is read by the name v0.7.0 gave it to, also where that name now resolves to another row. Several stored names of one model that disagree leave it unchecked, and `agentcompass doctor` lists them.
- **No launch passes a value through `cmd.exe`.** On Windows a `.cmd` or `.bat` launcher of a provider CLI is started as the program it runs, so no model name, prompt or path is parsed by `cmd.exe`. Values that come from reference data or discovery are checked against declared patterns before they reach a command line or a config fragment.
- **The tray asks less.** With nobody on the models page the tray asks the host for model lists every six hours instead of every ten minutes; the page still refreshes when opened. The strategy page labels the data date as "Data as of".

Values moved against v0.7.0: 118 cells of launch-table rows move by more than 0.5 standard units or 10 % (28 from taking the nearest declared version as the base, 29 from the `gpt-6-pro` definition and floor, 20 from reading effort shifts on the most correlated board). Level targets move with the panel member: creativity level 1 from -3.14 to -3.45 and level 2 from -1.96 to -2.14, execution level 2 from -1.19 to -0.89, design level 3 from 0.12 to 0.22.

Not in this release: provider-scoped identity for gateway catalogs (a name such as `deepseek-v4-pro` that DeepSeek's own endpoint now serves with newer weights is scored as the April row and listed as a gap). Not verified on a live account: launches of every provider CLI through the new launcher resolution, a launch of Gemini 4 Neon, and `data refresh --model` against a live board. No timed measurement of GPT-6 Pro in ChatGPT was found; the 600 s floor is a maintainer declaration.

The Windows tray installer is unsigned; Windows SmartScreen may warn on first launch. See [packaging/SIGNING.md](https://github.com/akiiwa-games/AgentCompass/blob/v0.7.1/packaging/SIGNING.md).

Status: alpha. Accounts come from discovery on your machine; choose which ones take part in the tray.
